title: Reliability ops activation slate and 30-90 sprint matrix
body:
Purpose: Working playbook for standing up a cross-functional reliability program focused on SLOs, error-budget governance, and predictable operational handoffs. This doc is intentionally tactical: quick checklists, sprint matrix, meeting rhythms and the minimum viable artifacts we need to onboard feature teams and partners. Notes to self and open questions are interleaved — this is a living drive doc, expect edits and short notes.

Executive summary (one-liner): Build a pragmatic, low-friction SLO activation path that routes teams from discovery -> SLO proposal -> canary -> production enforcement in 30-90 days with clear staffing, telemetry, and rollback criteria.

Goals (measurable):
- Onboard 6 feature teams to the SLO program in Q1 2027 with defined SLOs and runbooks.
- Reduce high-severity incident time-to-detect by 25% for instrumented services.
- Keep error budget burn-rate < 2x during major launches (initial 90-day target).
- Achieve 90% on-call runbook coverage for model-serving paths by end of sprint 3.

Audience: Platform engineering, SRE, Serving runtime, Product-hosted-api, Console, GTM/CS for customer communications.

Minimum artifacts per service to be accepted into program (MVP checklist):
- SLO brief (1-pager): service owner, customer-facing impact statement, SLI definitions, target values.
- Telemetry mapping: which Prometheus/Grafana dashboards + query IDs.
- Runbook: step-by-step triage with explicit rollback and fallback model variant actions.
- Ownership matrix: primary oncall, primary owner, escalation contact, secondary.
- Canary plan: traffic gating thresholds, success metrics, duration.

30-60-90 sprint cadence (high-level matrix):
- Sprint 0 (pre-work, week -2 to 0): discovery sessions, data readiness check, owner nominations, baseline SLIs.
- Sprint 1 (0–30 days): SLO briefs drafted, lightweight dashboards, runbook skeletons, smoke canary on staging (no prod traffic). Outcomes: 3 SLO briefs + dashboards.
- Sprint 2 (31–60 days): Canary in prod for low risk traffic slice, error budget thermostat installed (alerts at 25/50/75% burn), tabletop + dry-run. Outcomes: 3 canaries with rollback rehearsals.
- Sprint 3 (61–90 days): Full rollout to production, post-rollout evaluation, ops handoff, cadence integration into feature team rituals. Outcomes: program onboarding complete for cohort.

Cross-functional roster and roles (short):
- Program lead: Arielle Chen (coord, exec escalations)
- SRE coach: Diego Martinez (runbook reviews, alert tuning)
- Serving runtime SME: Priya Nair (fallback/quantization gating)
- Console/Observability: Ben Thompson (dashboards, alert wiring)
- Customer success liaison: Lina Ko (customer comms + incident impact summarization)

Communication & decision rhythm:
- Weekly sync: 30m, status, blockers, decisions required.
- SLO review: biweekly, review new SLO briefs and approve canary plans.
- Exec checkpoint: monthly, 15m summary for product and GTM leadership.
- Runbook dry-run: sprintly simulation with oncall rotation participants.

Alerting & governance rules (draft):
- Burn-rate thermostat: Pager at 50% burn over configured window OR 2x baseline burn over 1h -> immediate traffic freeze for canaries and mitigation window.
- Canary gating formula: pass if latency p95 < target AND error-rate < target for 15m sliding window; if fail -> automatic rollback and postmortem within 72h.
- SLA vs SLO comms: only escalate to customers for SLA breaches defined in contract; internal SLO breaches route through product & CS for customer-facing messaging decision.

Operational runbook patterns (examples to copy):
- Model-serving degraded-quality fallback: switch route to quantized-variant-A -> if errors persist, route to smaller-context model with reduced latency; if still degraded, return cached-responses and set incident severity.
- Capacity pressure play: auto-scale policy adjustments recipe + how to trigger reserved-capacity failover for Dedicated pools.

Risk register (top 6):
- Telemetry gaps (missing SLIs for newly containerized components).
- Owner bandwidth (feature teams overloaded -> SLO docs stall).
- Canary contamination (test data leaking to prod traffic slice).
- Cross-team coordination overhead (meeting fatigue leading to stalled rollouts).
- Cost spikes from aggressive canaries (uncapped traffic multiplier).
- Regulatory customer concerns on private deployments (need legal pre-approval path).

Open questions / work items (notes to self):
- Should we require a minimum error-budget reserve before a canary? (tradeoff: slower launches vs safety)
- Decide canonical SLO template fields for the one-pager.
- What is the expected engineering hours per onboarding? record baseline by cohort.
- Integrate cost telemetry into SLO dashboard (tokens/second + $/token delta).

Acceptance criteria for program sign-off: list of strings:
- Each onboarded service has an SLO brief, runbook, and connected metrics feed.
- Alerts wired to oncall rotations with playbook links embedded.
- One successful canary and one simulated rollback executed with postmortem.
- Stakeholder signoff from Product and CS templates completed.

Meeting prep checklist (for weekly sync):
- Owners: update sprint tile (what shipped, what blocked).
- Metrics: show current burn-rate and baseline from Grafana panel IDs.
- Risks: top 3 and mitigation status.

Appendix: quick templates to copy/paste (SLO brief outline, runbook header, canary checklist) — keep these in the program Confluence but reference IDs above. Also TODO to export the runbook examples into /runbooks/model-serving-runbooks in the repo.

Quick links for next edits: put a clean version of this doc into Confluence once the 1st cohort completes. Track onboarding time per team in JIRA ticket PLAT-9821; add a retrospective after sprint 3 to capture missing artifacts and improve the playbook.
